title: Hikari Currency (LUX) Valuation Theory:
abstract: We propose a complete valuation framework for Hikari Currency (LUX), a moral-execution-backed digital currency. LUX issuance is determined by the volume and quality of moral execution recorded in the Moral Execution Notebook (道徳実行ノート). LUX price is determined by a floating exchange rate model driven by the intensity of cosmic "Ma" (間) — measured in real time through IceCube neutrino GOLD alerts and ISP blazar Class-H activity.  Key results: - LUX issuance formula: `LUX = T × (1 + Q²)` where T = execution hours, Q = quality score (0–1) - LUX price range: 13.3 JPY – 265.1 JPY per LUX (20x floating band) - Primary driver of price variation: IceCube GOLD signalness (cosmic Ma intensity) - Theoretical basis: ΔP_Ma Hypothesis (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19706219–19720727) - Observational basis: 347-obj

title: The Hikari Card Protocol: A Performance-Scored Payment Card Framework Based on V=N/D
abstract: This paper introduces the **Hikari Card Protocol** — a payment card architecture in which each card carries a Performance Reactive Ink (PRI) layer that visually displays the card's cumulative V=N/D performance score (Value = Service / Friction). Unlike conventional payment cards, which are neutral conduits of monetary quantity, the Hikari Card is a carrier of monetary quality. The card's score is computed by the ubiquitous network at each transaction and returned as a visible color state on the card surface. The protocol is designed for immediate implementation on existing payment card infrastructure — magnetic stripe, IC chip, NFC — requiring only the addition of a PRI layer at the printing stage. title: Hikari Currency as Moral Density: A Framework for Quantifying Ethical Action as Economic Value
abstract: This paper proposes that Hikari Currency (LUX) is not merely a complementary currency but a formal mechanism for quantifying moral density — the accumulated ethical weight of human action — and converting it into transferable economic value. The core hypothesis is that moral action carries measurable N (value density) within the V=N/D framework, and that LUX serves as the unit of this measurement. This work connects Hiroi Chikuro's morality science (道徳科学) to contemporary economic theory through a formal valuation model.

title: The Ground-Cosmic Independence Test:
abstract: The Tendo Economics Two-Layer Framework assigns 60% weight to macro-economic ground conditions and 40% to KOKU-based cosmic timing. This weighting is only statistically justified if the two layers capture independent variance. This paper tests that independence using the complete IceCube GOLD-event dataset (2019–2025, N=53 usable intervals).  **Key findings:**  1. **KOKU × gold price (Ground Score proxy): r = +0.060** — Near-zero correlation. abstract: This paper documents and theorizes a specific category of human experience: the sudden, involuntary moment in which an individual consciousness perceives that it is structurally connected to the totality of existence. title: The Genki Universe Hypothesis: A Testable Prediction for Relativistic Jet Energy Output
abstract: This paper presents a falsifiable prediction derived from the Dual-Layer Universe theory (Koku-Genki model). We propose that the total energy output of relativistic jets contains an additional term beyond what is predicted by standard magnetohydrodynamic models (e.g., the Blandford–Znajek mechanism). This additional term, ΔP_間, arises from the energy gradient of the "間 (Ma)" — the Genki Universe layer — which is distinct from the geometric structure of spacetime (Koku Universe). We specify observable signatures that would confirm or refute this hypothesis using existing AGN and X-ray binary datasets.

title: Mass as Familiarity: A Genki-Particle Interpretation of Inertia in the KOKU Universe
abstract: This paper proposes a reinterpretation of mass (inertia) within the Genki-Particle / KOKU two-layer universe framework. The hypothesis is that mass is not an intrinsic property of matter but a relational property — the degree of a particle's "familiarity" (なじみ) with the Ma density field (ρ_Ma) of the KOKU layer. Particles with high familiarity resist displacement from their Ma density environment. This is inertia. Particles with low familiarity move freely through the KOKU layer. This is the behavior of neutrinos.

abstract: Classical physics proposed the luminiferous aether as a medium through which light propagates. The Michelson-Morley experiment (1887) disproved this model, and the aether was abandoned. title: Fukui as a Living Laboratory: Pre-Registered Protocol for Testing V=N/D Value Density Theory in Regional Economic Contexts
abstract: This paper presents Fukui Prefecture (福井県) as a proposed Living Laboratory for empirical testing of the V=N/D Value Density Theory. Fukui presents an unusual combination of characteristics — high happiness index rankings, low population density, strong traditional craft culture, and significant economic restructuring pressures — that make it an ideal site for testing whether V=N/D optimization (maximizing meaningful action per unit friction) produces measurably superior outcomes compared to GDP-optimizing economic strategies. A pre-registered experimental protocol is proposed.

title: Fukui as a Living Laboratory: Applying V=N/D Value Density Theory to Regional Civilizational Design
abstract: This paper proposes Fukui Prefecture, Japan, as an optimal living laboratory for the first regional-scale application of V=N/D theory (Value = Service Density / Friction). V=N/D proposes that individual and collective value is best measured by the density of service delivered relative to friction generated — a framework with implications for economic design, governance, education, and community structure. title: Fukui Experimental Protocol v1.0: Pre-Registered Failure Points for Regional V=N/D Implementation
abstract: This paper presents the pre-registered experimental protocol for a regional-scale implementation of V=N/D theory (Value = Service Density / Friction) in Fukui Prefecture, Japan. We document twelve pre-registered failure points (⑧–⑲), organized into five causal layers, that are predicted to emerge from the Fukui implementation. abstract: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule describes the relationship between electric current, magnetic field, and mechanical force in a conductor.
